claims.text: Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni high-entropy alloys in the proposed system are lightweight.
Optimized additive-manufacturing parameters can produce a high density of nano-twins in Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni HEAs.
Optimized additive manufacturing can refine the grain structure of Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni HEAs.
The conventionally wrought baseline has a lower nano-twin density than the additively manufactured state.
The conventionally wrought baseline has a coarser grain structure than the additively manufactured state.
Twin boundaries impede dislocation motion and thereby increase yield strength.
Grain refinement increases the mechanical strength of the alloy.
Nano-twins and refined grain boundaries act as preferential nucleation sites for an oxide scale.
The oxide scale nucleated at these microstructural features is coherent, protective, and slow growing.
Formation of the proposed protective oxide scale limits high-temperature oxidation.
Formation of the proposed protective oxide scale improves corrosion resistance.
The high-twin-density additively manufactured alloy will have higher yield strength than the wrought baseline.
The high-twin-density additively manufactured alloy will show lower oxidation weight gain at 700°C in air than the wrought baseline.
The high-twin-density additively manufactured alloy will have better accelerated-corrosion performance than the wrought baseline.
Post-processing annealing can reduce the nano-twin density.
Reducing nano-twin density by annealing will decrease mechanical strength.
Reducing nano-twin density by annealing will worsen oxidation and corrosion resistance.
Thermal exposure above the stability limit of the nano-twinned structure will substantially reduce twin-boundary density and eliminate its proposed dual benefits.
